registry.description: Anguish is the experience of being pressed, compressed, squeezed — the inner state of distress when circumstances close in from every side and there is no room to breathe. The Hebrew roots carry images of constriction, writhing, and the pangs of labour; the vocabulary overlaps with distress, grief, and sorrow. What marks anguish is the quality of being trapped: not simply sorrowful but hemmed in with nowhere to turn. It appears across the full range of human crisis — exile, bereavement, defeat, illness — and in the cry to God from within it.
